q: Does end-to-end re-assembly from the raw MiSeq reads (764x coverage, if the SRA is available) reproduce the deposited MN718463 assembly at the same 45,089 bp / 28.72% GC / 66-CDS resolution, or does it expose an assembler-version dependency?
basis: This replication started from the deposited assembly (MN718463), not from raw reads. Genome-statistics agreement therefore inherits any assembly-level miscall. The paper specifies SPAdes 3.13.0 (2019-era); modern SPAdes versions and alternate assemblers (Unicycler, Flye+polish) may yield subtly different contig boundaries, terminal-repeat resolution, or minor indel calls in low-complexity regions of the 28.7%-GC phage.
next_steps: Query SRA/ENA for reads linked to BioProject/BioSample of MN718463 or CD34-Sr host; if absent, contact corresponding author (Hinc/Obuchowski, Medical University of Gdansk).
Rerun SPAdes 3.13.0 (original) and SPAdes >=3.15 for direct comparison; also run Unicycler and Flye with short-read polishing.
Diff assemblies with dnadiff (MUMmer) and quast; report any SNPs, indels, or terminal-region differences vs MN718463.
Publish per-assembler assembly + diff table in evidence/ as reads_to_assembly_replication.tsv.

q: Do modern viral gene-annotation pipelines (pharokka, PHASTER, VIBRANT, Prokka+PHROG HMMs) reproduce the paper's 37 functionally annotated ORFs, or is the sparser 9-CDS functional annotation in the GenBank deposit actually closer to a modern re-analysis?
basis: Claim C6 (37/66 ORFs with predicted function via myRAST v36) was only partially tested here because myRAST v36 versioning/availability is unreliable (the RAST ecosystem has migrated repeatedly). The 37-vs-9 discrepancy between paper and deposit is unresolved and matters for downstream comparative work.
next_steps: Run pharokka (PHROG-based, current best-practice for phage annotation) on MN718463; count functionally annotated CDS.
Run PHASTER and VIBRANT for cross-tool agreement.
If myRAST/RAST is reachable via the KBase or PATRIC/BV-BRC portals, rerun that specific version-lineage as well.

Produce a 66-row CDS-by-CDS annotation matrix (paper vs deposit vs pharokka vs PHASTER vs VIBRANT) as evidence/annotation_delta.tsv; identify which named modules (terminase, portal, capsid, integrase, holin, etc.) are call-consistent.

q: Have any Clostridioides difficile phage genomes deposited after 2021 (post-paper) joined the same ICTV genus as phiCDKH01 / phiCD24-1, and if so, do they weaken the paper's 'closest relative is phiCD24-1' framing or shift the genus's species-level boundaries?
basis: The novelty claim (C9) was tested against an 11-phage panel selected from pre-2021 literature. New C. difficile phage genomes are continually deposited; a congeneric relative deposited after 2021 could alter both the closest-relative identity and the genus-level VIRIDIC clustering. The paper's 'novel species in a genus with only phiCD24-1' framing is time-sensitive.
next_steps: Query NCBI taxonomy/nucleotide for all Clostridioides difficile phage genomes (host=Clostridioides difficile, molecule=DNA, seq-length 20-200 kb) with deposit dates 2021-01-01 to present.
Compute VIRIDIC-style whole-genome intergenomic identity of each post-2021 phage vs phiCDKH01 and vs phiCD24-1.
Rebuild the intergenomic-identity matrix including the extended panel; reapply ICTV thresholds (genus 70%, species 95%).
Report any newly congeneric or conspecific phages in evidence/genus_expansion_2026.tsv; if any conspecific relatives are found, flag as material update to the paper's novelty claim.

q: Do the 5 CRISPR spacers detected on phiCDKH01 have identifiable protospacer targets in currently known Clostridioides difficile strains, other C. difficile phages, or C. difficile mobile elements (plasmids, ICEs) --- i.e., can a biological function or evolutionary origin be inferred for this intra-phage CRISPR array?
basis: The paper reports the CRISPR array as a genomic feature (5 spacers of 35/36/37 bp, exactly reproduced here by minced) but does not analyze what the spacers target. Intra-phage CRISPR arrays are unusual and potentially informative about phage-phage competition, superinfection exclusion, or horizontal-gene-transfer suppression in the C. difficile pan-genome.
next_steps: Extract the 5 spacer sequences from evidence/crispr_phiCDKH01.txt.

BLASTn each spacer against (a) NCBI nt restricted to Clostridioides difficile taxid 1496, (b) all C. difficile phage genomes in the extended panel, (c) NCBI plasmid RefSeq restricted to Firmicutes hosts.
Also search PHASTER/pharokka-predicted prophage regions inside C. difficile chromosomes for protospacers.
Report protospacer hits (>=90% identity across full spacer with a canonical PAM) in evidence/crispr_spacer_targets.tsv; interpret in the context of phage-phage exclusion or anti-plasmid activity.

q: Is the 39-bp discrepancy in the reported prophage integration coordinates (paper: 288,650-333,698 in JACSDL010000003.1; this replication: 288,611-333,698) an attL/attR attachment-site convention difference, or does it reflect a real coordinate disagreement --- and can the exact tRNA/attB integration site in the C. difficile host chromosome be identified?
basis: BLASTn placed the prophage at 288,611-333,698 vs the paper's 288,650-333,698: right endpoint agrees exactly, left endpoint differs by 39 bp. Temperate siphoviruses typically integrate at tRNA loci with short direct repeats (attL/attR); the 39-bp offset is plausibly a boundary-convention difference (does one include the direct repeat, the other not?) but was not investigated.
next_steps: Extract the ~200 bp flanking each candidate prophage boundary in JACSDL010000003.1.
Search for direct repeats (attL/attR) using standard tools (Phaster attachment-site detector, or manual pairwise BLAST of the two flanks).
Annotate the host locus adjacent to the integration site with prokka/RAST; check whether integration is into a tRNA gene (canonical for many temperate phages) or a coding gene.
Report the attB/attL/attR coordinates, direct-repeat sequence, and host feature at the integration site in evidence/attachment_site_analysis.tsv; reconcile the 39-bp offset explicitly.
